adn_tx.t: Alaska agrees with, but does not join, Texas lawsuit seeking to overturn presidential election — Anchorage Daily News (2020-12-09)

checks.legal: CourtListener was blocked. Alaska CourtView was not searched directly. Searched news (ADN, Alaska Beacon, Alaska Public Media, Juneau Independent, KTUU) and Wikipedia for lawsuits, ethics complaints and APOC actions. Found the APOC tenant-disclosure matter (2025 order, 2026 recommendation, disqualification and reinstatement) and the self-funding-limit issue. No lawsuit or criminal matter found; the Beacon noted no state or federal suit by Taylor over the self-funding cap.
checks.foreign: No foreign ties found in news or his pamphlet. Exact-name check of the DOJ FARA bulk files (registrants, short forms, foreign principals), searched 2026-10-13: no row names this candidate (only hit: a 'Taylor Fontan' at Sher Tremonte LLP — not him).
checks.claims: Campaign site tregforak.com could not be fetched (tool provenance block). As a stand-in, used his candidate-authored Official Election Pamphlet statement (all bio claims) plus two campaign statements on the APOC disputes. No ad scripts were found. Seven claims: 4 rated (unverifiable excluded): 1 true, 2 partly, 1 misleading; 3 unverifiable.
checks.democracy: Never in Congress. Searched news and Wikipedia for statements on 2020/2024 presidential results; none found. AG-era election litigation not reviewed.

research_notes: FARA changed only. On Dec. 9, 2020 the Alaska Department of Law declined to join Texas v. Pennsylvania while saying it agreed election integrity needs review, and called the national election 'free and fair' (ADN). The article names no AG; Taylor became AG in 2021, so this is NOT attributed to him. His own AG-era election litigation is still unreviewed. CourtListener, Justia, Senate eFD, House/Senate Ethics, APOC and Alaska CourtView were all unreachable from this environment (proxy 403 / fetch provenance block), so no court or ethics database was searched directly.
